time_limits: Each timeout is when waiting stops. Ending every process of that context then takes at most cleanup_bound_seconds more, inside one absolute deadline: SIGTERM first to the launcher of the context alone, so that torchrun closes its own workers in order; then to every process of the invocation still running; then SIGKILL to whoever is still running, including workers in sessions of their own. The three steps and their waits are in the script and together stay inside the bound. Only processes of that invocation are signalled. A construction context therefore ends within 90 s and the torchrun dry run within 300 s, cleanup included: 750 s for the six contexts, and 150 s of the 900 s allocation remain for launcher, parent, I/O and provenance. Inside the dry run torchrun gets rank_entry_timeout_seconds less the cleanup bound, less 20 s kept for the report, less the time the preparation took, so its bound always expires before the parent's; it is not started with fewer than 30 s. A context reports an error, and the report gives no reading, also when processes outlived it and had to be ended or survived the cleanup. Lowered on 05/11/2026 from 90 s and 300 s of waiting, after the review of GPT (R-TIMEOUT), to keep the cleanup inside the declared limits.
